text:
alex.k: heads-up — I'm about to create a new GPU nodepool in us-west1 for batch-infer workloads. planning A10G mixed with T4 for cheaper spot bursts. anyone see quota or networking gotchas?

maria_ops: +1 on A10G for perf, T4 for cost. double-check regional GPU quotas with cloud console first. last time we hit a per-project regional limit. :grimacing:

ryan_sre: what scale are you planning? initial sizes? autoscaler behaviour matters a lot for these jobs.

alex.k: starting target: min 0, max 50 nodes. node size 1GPU per node (a10g-2g?). we need burst capacity but keep preemptible/spot for cost.

anya_mlinfra: prefer pinned small instances for latency-sensitive routes, but batch can be spot. are these nodes going to be tainted for specific workloads? will pods use gpu resource requests?

alex.k: yes taint: dedicated=gpu:NoSchedule. pods will have tolerations and requests: requests: nvidia.com/gpu: 1. also adding nodeAffinity for batch namespace.

maria_ops: reminder — cluster-autoscaler + GPU special cases: scale down delays if pods have local storage, and CA might ignore nodes if pod can't be reprovisioned due to nodeSelector. configure expander and balance-similar-node-groups?

ryan_sre: add these CA flags: --skip-nodes-with-system-pods=false and --balance-similar-node-groups=true. also set scale-down-unneeded-time to 10m for bursty loads.

alex.k: good call. I'm going to run a preflight script to validate quotas & IAM. posting snippet:

```
# check GPU quotas
gcloud compute regions describe us-west1 --format="json(quotas)" | jq '.quotas[] | select(.metric|test("GPUS"))'
# quick kube check
kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep gpu || true
```

maria_ops: also check service account has compute.viewer and iam.serviceAccounts.actAs for the node pool creation. and confirm KMS key access if we're using encrypted disks.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot created ticket INFRA-4921: "us-west1 gpu nodepool preflight" assigned to @alex.k, due 2h.

alex.k: ran quota check — looks like we have 40 GPUs available in us-west1 for A10 family, 100 for T4. That 40 is a hard limiter unless we request quota increase.

anya_mlinfra: then for max 50 nodes using 1 A10 each we'd need 50 A10 quota — so either mix types or set max nodes to 40. mixing T4 spot for the remainder seems safest.

ryan_sre: networking: ensure routes and firewall allow egress to our artifact registry and metrics backend. last provisioning had nodes in a subnet with restricted egress and kubelet failed pulling GCR images.

alex.k: noted. subnet has NAT gateway but it's on a different subnetwork than our control plane. I will add a route and update NAT tags.

maria_ops: watch out for IP exhaustion if we set max 50 in smaller subnet. use /22 or expand secondary ip range.

alex.k: changing nodepool config to use larger secondary range. also enabling node-local-dns?

ryan_sre: enable node-local-dns for reduced DNS latency and fewer egress to DNS. for CA, ensure node group autoscaling uses proper labels so scale-down doesn't evict eviction-prone pods: add annotation cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/safe-to-evict=true for batch pods?

anya_mlinfra: we generally mark batch pods as not safe-to-evict because of checkpointing, but we can add short checkpointing to be evictable. which will improve scale-down.

alex.k: change of plan: create two nodepools: gpu-burst-spot (T4 preemptible, max 20) and gpu-stable (A10 reserved, max 40, min 1). autoscaler policies: gpu-stable prefer non-preemptible.

maria_ops: For GCP: use --preemptible flag for node template. For reserved, set node auto-repair and upgrade strategy. and tag gpu-stable nodes with label pool=stable-gpu for billing.

alex.k: creating pool now — paste create command:

```
gcloud container node-pools create gpu-stable \
  --cluster=prod-cluster \
  --region=us-west1 \
  --machine-type=n1-standard-16 \
  --accelerator=type=a10g,count=1 \
  --min-nodes=1 --max-nodes=40 \
  --node-labels=dedicated=gpu,pool=stable-gpu \
  --node-taints=dedicated=gpu:NoSchedule \
  --enable-autoscaling
```

ryan_sre: make sure to set --workload-metadata=GKE_METADATA or GCE_METADATA per our security baseline. also add --service-account=infra-node-sa@redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com

alex.k: command executed. initial nodes provisioning. I see a quota error on pool creation for A10 count: "Quota 'GPUS_ALL_REGIONS' exceeded".

maria_ops: ack — please open a quota increase request with cloud support; include expected sustained usage and billing justification. we can temporarily lower A10 max to 20 and lean on T4 for rest.

alex.k: lowered max to 20 and recreated. pool is up with 4 nodes ready. kube labels look good.

anya_mlinfra: run a quick smoke test with a GPU job and verify CUDA driver + nvidia-device-plugin.

alex.k: smoke: ran a short TF job — container sees 1 GPU. nvidia-smi returns A10, drivers present. test logs: "Allocated 1/1 GPUs".

ryan_sre: add alerting: nodepool GPU usage > 80% for 10m -> paging, and node provisioning failures -> pager. also chart cost per-hour for A10 vs T4 in dashboards.

maria_ops: will add budget alerts for us-west1 GPU spend. also add ticket to request A10 quota bump for long term.

alex.k: thanks all. follow-ups: I will patch CA flags, open quota ticket, and spin up gpu-burst-spot pool next. any objections?

anya_mlinfra: none. please tag us in the ticket and post results here. :rocket:

ryan_sre: no objections. keep an eye on scale down flapping in first 24h.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot updated ticket INFRA-4921: status -> in_progress.

alex.k: closing loop — final note to docs: I'll add a short runbook for creating GPU nodepools (taints, CA flags, quota checklist, NAT/subnet notes).
